newsitem.title: JAPAN: Thai finance, foreign ministers to visit Japan.
newsitem.headline: Thai finance, foreign ministers to visit Japan.

text.p: Thailand's newly-installed finance minister and foreign minister will visit Japan next week for planned meetings with Japanese monetary officials and bankers, a Thai embassy official in Tokyo said on Tuesday.
Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya and Foreign Minister Prachuab Chaiyasarn will be in Tokyo from July 17 to 18 for an unofficial visit, the embassy official said.

She said Thanong planned to meet Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka and also separately meet Japanese private bankers, but added that the meetings had not yet been fixed. She said Thanong may also meet Bank of Japan Governor Yasuo Matsushita.

Thanong, previously a little-known banker, was appointed Thailand's finance minister on June 20 after the much-respected Amnuay Viravan resigned from the post over policy differences with political rivals in the government.
Last week, Thailand sent markets into a frenzy by announcing a de facto devaluation of the Thai baht, sending the the Thai currency 15 to 20 percent lower on the surprise move to float the baht.

Thailand held a massive 12.935 trillion yen ($114 billion) in yen-denominated loans from the Japanese government as of end-March 1996. A weaker baht means the Thai government needs to raise additional money to pay back the yen debt to Tokyo.

Japanese investors have cut back their exposure to Thailand, with Thai stock and bond holdings by Japanese investment trusts totalling 93.14 billion yen ($824 million) at the end of April, the latest figure available, compared to 121.95 billion yen ($1.07 billion) at the end of August 1996.
An official at the Japanese finance ministry said he had not been notified of the meeting between the finance ministers.
